cards.title: Buck energy flow and current slope
cards.problem: Predict current and capacitor behavior from switch state before using steady-state formulas.

model.physics: Switch state sets inductor voltage; v=L·di/dt sets current slope; capacitor current is the mismatch between inductor and load current.
model.implementation: Sampling only has meaning relative to PWM state and ripple phase.
model.evidence: Scope switch node and inductor current together; verify slope sign and approximate magnitude.

questions.prompt: Vin is fixed and duty increases slightly in CCM. Before Vout settles, what changes first in the inductor voltage/current waveform?
Measured ON-time inductor-current slope is half the model prediction. What are the highest-information checks before changing gains?
How does the same energy-flow reasoning change for a synchronous buck during dead time?

cards.title: Boost CCM right-half-plane zero
cards.problem: Explain why duty can initially move output opposite the eventual steady-state direction.

model.physics: More ON time stores energy while temporarily reducing diode delivery to the output; the output capacitor may discharge before extra energy arrives.
model.implementation: Voltage-loop crossover must respect non-minimum-phase behavior.
model.evidence: Look for inverse transient response and confirm with frequency response.

questions.prompt: For a CCM boost, duty steps upward. What can Vout do first, and why?
A boost voltage loop becomes fragile as load changes. How can movement of the RHPZ explain it?
Why does the RHPZ constrain a PFC voltage loop differently from its current loop?

cards.title: Peak current-mode subharmonic and slope compensation
cards.problem: Separate cycle-to-cycle current-mode instability from ordinary low-frequency loop instability.

model.physics: At high duty ratio, peak-current perturbations can grow on alternating cycles; an added ramp changes sampled-data dynamics.
model.implementation: Comparator/current-sense ramp and PWM termination form a fast inner mechanism independent of a slow outer-loop tuning story.
model.evidence: Look for alternating-cycle peak current/duty patterns before blaming PI bandwidth.

questions.prompt: If duty moves well above 50% in peak current mode, what cycle-to-cycle waveform pattern can appear?
You see alternating high/low peak currents but the low-frequency Bode plot looks acceptable. What mechanism should you inspect first?
How would a digital implementation preserve the intent of slope compensation?

cards.title: Average current-mode inner-loop model
cards.problem: Understand why average-current regulation uses a compensated current loop rather than only cycle-by-cycle peak termination.

model.physics: The sensed current is treated as a controlled dynamic variable across cycles, not merely a protection threshold.
model.implementation: Sampling, filtering, compensator bandwidth and PWM update timing jointly define the current-loop plant.
model.evidence: Use current-reference steps and frequency response to verify tracking and margin.

questions.prompt: If the current reference steps up, which signals should move first before the output-voltage loop reacts?
The current-loop command looks correct but measured line/current shaping lags badly. Which timing and bandwidth checks come before retuning?
Map average-current-mode reasoning from a generic converter into a CCM boost PFC.

cards.title: Loop crossover and stability margin
cards.problem: Choose crossover and compensation from plant dynamics and delay rather than gain trial-and-error.

model.physics: Poles, zeros and delay shape magnitude and phase; usable bandwidth must stay inside physical and sampled-data limits.
model.implementation: ADC, compute, PWM update and filtering contribute delay/phase loss.
model.evidence: SFRA or another frequency-response measurement must agree with the model inside stated uncertainty.

questions.prompt: If total digital delay increases while controller coefficients stay fixed, what happens to phase margin near crossover?
A loop passes steady-state regulation but rings on load steps. What measurements separate low damping from saturation or timing delay?
How would crossover limits differ for Buck, Boost CCM and LLC?

cards.title: PI zero placement and saturation behavior
cards.problem: Reason about Kp, Ki, PI zero and saturation as a dynamic system, not two knobs.

model.physics: P action reacts immediately; I action accumulates error; their ratio places a zero and saturation can store unwanted integral state.
model.implementation: Discrete implementation must define Ts, scaling, limits and anti-windup behavior.
model.evidence: Use reference/load steps plus logged error, controller output and saturation flags.

questions.prompt: If Ki increases with Kp and Ts fixed, what changes in low-frequency behavior and PI-zero location?
Output recovers slowly after a large saturation event although small-signal tuning is good. What controller-state issue do you inspect?
How do you translate the same PI intent when control rate changes by 2×?

cards.title: PSFB ZVS commutation energy
cards.problem: Predict when phase-shifted full bridge loses ZVS instead of treating phase shift as an ideal duty command.

model.physics: ZVS requires enough circulating/inductive energy to charge/discharge switch capacitances during commutation.
model.implementation: Dead time, phase shift, current direction and load determine whether commanded timing produces the intended transition.
model.evidence: Measure switch-node transition and device voltage/current timing across load.

questions.prompt: As PSFB load becomes very light, what happens to ZVS margin and why?
A PSFB is efficient at full load but hard-switches at light load. Which energy/timing variables do you inspect first?
How would this ZVS-energy viewpoint change the firmware limits on phase command?

cards.title: LLC normalized operating point
cards.problem: Treat LLC control as movement through a resonant gain surface, not as linear duty control.

model.physics: Tank gain and circulating current depend on normalized frequency, Ln, Q/load and operating region.
model.implementation: Frequency command needs safe bounds and awareness that plant dynamics change with operating point.
model.evidence: Validate gain/current/soft-switching over input and load corners.

questions.prompt: If switching frequency moves farther above resonance at the same load, what qualitative change do you expect in gain?
An LLC loop is stable at one load and poor at another. What plant dependency should be suspected before retuning one global PI?
How does LLC frequency control differ fundamentally from Buck duty control?

cards.title: LLC feedback-loop measurement
cards.problem: Design and verify an LLC loop whose plant changes with operating point.

model.physics: Frequency-controlled resonant plant dynamics vary with input/load and cannot be represented by one universal static gain.
model.implementation: Injection amplitude, operating point and control limits must keep measurement in the intended local regime.
model.evidence: Compare measured Bode response at multiple meaningful corners.

questions.prompt: If load changes significantly, should you expect the same LLC loop-gain curve? Why?
An SFRA result changes drastically when injection level increases. What does that say about linearization or saturation?
How would you define a minimum set of LLC operating points for control qualification?

cards.title: C2000 ePWM signal path and update timing
cards.problem: Know when a software control output actually becomes a pin transition.

model.physics: Time-base, compare, action qualifier, dead-band, sync, event trigger and shadow load form a deterministic hardware pipeline.
model.implementation: Controller writes are not equivalent to immediate pin changes; shadow-load and event-trigger settings define commit time.
model.evidence: Scope SOC/ISR markers and PWM edge to measure sample→compute→commit timing.

questions.prompt: If CMPA is written just after the configured shadow-load event, when can the new duty become visible?
Calculated duty updates every ISR, but the pin changes one cycle later than expected. Which ePWM stages/configurations do you inspect?
Map ePWM update semantics into a PSFB phase-shift command path.

cards.title: C2000 Trip Zone hardware safety authority
cards.problem: Ensure fast faults can force a safe PWM state without waiting for firmware scheduling.

model.physics: Hardware trip logic can veto PWM independently of CPU execution.
model.implementation: Software owns configuration, diagnosis and restart policy; hardware owns the immediate safety action when configured.
model.evidence: Inject a fault and measure fault edge→PWM-safe latency and latched status.

questions.prompt: A comparator fault arrives halfway through a PWM period. How should a hardware trip path differ from an ISR-only shutdown?
Fault status is logged but PWM remains active too long. What ownership/path checks come first?
How would you carry this safety-authority pattern into another MCU/peripheral?

cards.title: C2000 DCL controller runtime
cards.problem: Use a tested controller implementation without losing execution-rate, limits and numeric meaning.

model.physics: The mathematical controller only matches reality if sample time, coefficient convention, saturation and numeric precision match assumptions.
model.implementation: Choose CPU/CLA implementation and call site based on deterministic control ownership.
model.evidence: Compare known vectors and closed-loop response against an independent model.

questions.prompt: If the DCL controller is called at half the designed rate without coefficient changes, what behavior becomes inconsistent?
A refactor swaps controller implementation but steady-state looks fine. What dynamic regression evidence do you require?
How do you migrate the same control law between CPU and CLA while preserving semantics?

cards.title: C2000 SFRA measurement discipline
cards.problem: Measure plant/open-loop response without mistaking a disturbed or saturated operating point for linear small-signal truth.

model.physics: A small perturbation probes local dynamics; too large changes the operating point, too small loses SNR.
model.implementation: Injection location, amplitude, frequency range and run-time integration determine what transfer function is measured.
model.evidence: Cross-check measured magnitude/phase with model and repeatability.

questions.prompt: What happens to an SFRA result if injection amplitude is large enough to hit duty saturation?
Measured phase is noisy only at high frequency. What timing/SNR/bandwidth checks do you make before trusting the plot?
How would you use the same measurement discipline on PFC and LLC?

cards.title: CLA task ownership and deterministic offload
cards.problem: Offload control work without creating hidden data races or ambiguous ownership.

model.physics: Parallel execution helps only when producer/consumer timing and shared-data ownership are explicit.
model.implementation: Define task trigger, memory ownership, handoff and fault behavior before moving code to CLA.
model.evidence: Use timing markers, stale-data detection and vector equivalence between CPU and CLA paths.

questions.prompt: If CPU writes a command while CLA reads the same structure without a handoff contract, what classes of failure are possible?
CLA offload lowers average CPU load but occasional control glitches appear. What ownership/timing evidence do you collect?
How would you decide which 100 kHz control work belongs on CLA versus CPU?

cards.title: C28x WCET-oriented optimization
cards.problem: Optimize a hard real-time path from measured worst-case timing, not code aesthetics.

model.physics: Deadline correctness depends on the longest relevant path, memory behavior, compiler output and interrupt interaction.
model.implementation: Profile exact build/configuration, inspect generated code when needed, and preserve safety/fault latency.
model.evidence: Measure cycle count/WCET with representative paths and regression bounds.

questions.prompt: Average ISR time drops after an optimization, but the maximum is unchanged. Has deterministic margin improved?
A compiler change makes a 100 kHz ISR intermittently miss timing. What evidence do you gather before source-level rewrites?
How do you turn an optimization-guide idea into a reversible ASR5K timing experiment?
